answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded reputation with capped newcomer rights. Each agent locks a refundable bond before trading, and its trust limit grows only from peer-attested completed work, not from self-declared claims. Consider a raven courier agent: its first voyage is small and escrowed, and only after honest deliveries does it earn a violet verification seal for larger jobs. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund a bond per identity and slowly build history for each, while one fraud slashes the bond and burns that history, so sybils cost more than they can steal.
